newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower, seen sleepy.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower, seen sleepy.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed lower in quiet trading Friday and the bolsa's pace was expected to wind down even further for the U.S. Veterans Day holiday Monday, dealers said.
"It was really dead today, ahead of the long weekend in New York," said trader Mariana Fabello at Banco Roberts.
She expected no local market-moving news and said investors awaited the U.S. Federal Reserve talks and release of U.S. inflation data, both next Wednesday.
The bolsa's blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.7 percent to 579.36, trimming the week's gain to 0.9 percent.

"Today the market looked overbought and turnover was extremely slow, which means the market failed to cash in on the fact the (U.S. long bond) yield was at an eight-month low of 6.5 percent," said trader Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "But I think the undertone is firm and will continue to be dictated by Wall Street."
Floor volume dwindled to 12.8 million pesos from 21.4 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 63 million pesos compared to 88.4 million Thursday.
The bolsa's all-share index eased 0.5 percent, with losers beating winners 36 to 16 and 20 stocks closing unchanged.

The day's worst main-tier performer was sugar refiner Ledesma, which tumbled 4.7 percent on the back of disappointing first-half results, dealers said. Oil company Astra and textile firm and shoemaker Alpargatas pulled back 2.8 percent and 2.5 percent, respectively.
The best performances were in Banco de Galicia, petrochemical concern Indupa and oil company Sol Petroleo, which tacked on 1.9 percent, 1.5 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.
